payload.code:
The class functions also allow us to chart inheritance relationships. We can find the
parent of a class, for example, with get_parent_class(). This function requires either
an object or a class name, and it returns the name of the superclass, if any. If no such
class exists—that is, if the class we are testing does not have a parent—then the function
returns false.

// listing 05.53
print  get_parent_class('\\popp\\ch04\\batch02\\BookProduct');

payload.markdown: As you might expect, this yields the parent class: ShopProduct.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Functions: Reusable blocks of code that take arguments and return values.
Inheritance: Deriving a class from a base class to reuse and specialise its behaviour.
Interfaces: A pure contract of method signatures with no implementation.
SPL Structures: PHP's built-in data structures and interfaces such as ArrayObject and SplStack.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Arrow Functions: fn() => expressions: closures with automatic by-value capture.

    print "BookProduct is a subclass of ShopProduct\n";
}
